body.x: Water Eyes Co., Ltd. (CEO Yeonwuk Jung) announced its participation in CES 2025, which will take place from January 7 to 10 in Las Vegas. The company will exhibit at the K-Startup Pavilion and showcase its innovative wastewater management solutions.

Founded in 2020 as part of the Korea Water Resources Corporation’s internal venture program, Water Eyes has focused on developing AI-driven solutions to address global environmental challenges. Dedicated to leading the creation and expansion of "Smart Water Cities," the company integrates cutting-edge technology with sustainability. Through collaborative research with renowned international universities, Water Eyes has tailored solutions for specific regions, including Vietnam and the Middle East, to foster positive global change.

At CES 2025, Water Eyes will unveil its Intelligent Water Eyes for Wastewater, a comprehensive water quality management platform comprising real-time measurement sensors, an AI-based correlation analysis system, a cloud server, and a mobile application.

This platform digitizes various indicators generated during wastewater treatment, enabling real-time data collection and optimization of the entire process. It helps reduce energy and chemical inputs required for treatment, offering a cost-efficient and sustainable solution.

The platform distinguishes itself by employing AI algorithms to deliver predictive data, enabling proactive problem identification and early intervention. This approach prioritizes mitigating risks before issues escalate, providing operators with critical insights for efficient decision-making.

The compact design of Intelligent Water Eyes for Wastewater is approximately 90% smaller than similar systems, allowing for easy installation and usability. Its reduced size enhances the real-time measurement of high-concentration wastewater, making it more accessible to various facilities.

A Water Eyes representative explained, “For a single wastewater treatment facility, our solution can reduce the annual cost of chemicals for water quality improvement by up to 70% and blower operation electricity costs by as much as 40%. This equates to an annual reduction of up to 45,000 tons of carbon emissions, demonstrating exceptional sustainability benefits.”

The company also highlighted plans to explore Official Development Assistance (ODA) projects in Vietnam and Southeast Asia, aiming to expand its international presence through collaborations with domestic conglomerates. “CES 2025 will serve as a pivotal platform to showcase the excellence of our technology, enhance brand recognition, and accelerate business opportunities ahead of our global market entry,” the representative added.

AVING News, covering CES for 19 consecutive years, continues to bridge the gap for Korean SMEs and startups looking to expand globally. AVING will host its Broadcasting Zone at the Venetian Expo, featuring the CES Media Day Startup Conference and global media interviews to promote Korean startups worldwide. AVING's international media partners will cover these programs.
